subject: octopus
pitch: A curious reef octopus in coral and rust tones, covered in little bumps and paler mottling. A soft, bulbous head, golden eyes with bar-shaped pupils and a slightly grumpy brow. Its eight arms curl out in every direction, each lined with rows of cream suckers, and one arm proudly holds up an old brass key it found on a shipwreck.
reasoning:
I'm planning an octopus model resting on the floor with a bulbous mantle, sized realistically at roughly 0.3m body with 0.6-1m arms, and starting to lay out the skeleton structure with a root body joint.

I'm now working through the spine chain details — placing joints via catmull points and defining radii for the bulbous mantle shape, then setting up a root joint, a named spine chain, and planning the head with a beak/jaw, eight radiating arm chains (one raised holding the key), and eyes positioned near the front of the head with sphere pupils.

Positioning the pupil along the eye direction, then working out the brow geometry and orientation so the inner edge tilts down for a grumpy look, using direction and up vectors to control the tilt.

Now placing the brow as a small beveled box near the eye, then positioning the beak geometry beneath the head where the arms converge, with the upper beak as a small cone attached to a jaw joint parented under the first spine.

Mapping out the 8 radial arms evenly spaced around the body base, each defined as a curved path of points moving outward from the body with increasing radius and a slight curl, so the arms lie flat near the base but lift upward at the tips.

I'm tuning the arm heights so the lowest points just touch the floor, then setting one arm apart as the raised arm holding the key high above the body, sketching its direction and rise toward the top.

Now I'm plotting the raised arm's curve from base to tip, with the radius tapering as it climbs, and positioning the key at the tip with a torus bow, cylindrical shaft, and bit boxes so it looks like the arm is gripping the shaft near the top.

Still computing wrap geometry...

Setting shaft radius at 0.014 and circle hug radius around 0.032. For the chains, I'm structuring each arm as a joint chain parented to root, with 5 joints for regular arms and 7 for the raised arm, naming them systematically and starting the first joint at the arm base position.

Now I'm defining the sweep paint: a mottled coral-and-rust base with paler mottled spots overlaid, countershaded with a peach belly, cream sucker undersides on the arms, and scattered small rust bumps across the mantle and arms.

For the suckers, I'm weighing where to place them along each arm's sweep so they're visible given the octopus pose—since arms rest near the floor, placing suckers directly underneath would hide them, so I'm leaning toward positioning them at upward-facing side angles (around ±60°) so the characteristic rows read clearly from above.

Adding sucker geometry...

Now I'm shaping the mantle skin by sweeping along the spine chain, leaning it backward behind the head with a tapering elliptical radius profile from base to tail tip.

I'm also tightening the overall height so the model stays proportional, then adding a webbed skirt ring around the arm bases using a lathe disc to connect the arms visually.

For the eyes, I'll attach them to the second spine joint and build an eye socket by adding a flattened rust-colored mound beneath each eyeball sphere, partially embedding the eye for a more sculpted look.

Still placing eye geometry...

For the brow, I'm positioning it slightly above and offset from the eye so it overlaps the sphere just enough to read as a lid. For the mouth, I'm checking where the jaw joint and body radius put the front edge, trying to figure out a beak position that sits naturally near the arm base rather than hidden beneath the body.

Placing upper and lower beak cones angled toward each other with dark brownish tones, sized small and tipped forward-down to resemble a beak shape.

I'm considering adding a tiny siphon funnel on the mantle side but deciding to skip it, then moving to design a brass key with patina coloring—shaft as a thin cylinder and bow as a small torus, attached to the last joint of the raised arm's chain.

Now I'm working out the key's bit geometry, placing small boxes near the shaft's bottom to form the teeth, and adjusting their position and size so they sit just below where the arm wraps around the shaft.

Computing the arm's path geometry along its sweep—origin, radial direction, and perpendicular offsets—to place each point of the raised arm's chain as it curves up toward the shaft.

Mapping out the spiral endpoint to join the arm points together, then sketching coordinate sequences for curled arm paths with a side-offset factor to control left/right bending along each limb.

I'm fixing the raised arm to be front-left with its own azimuth while spreading the remaining arms evenly around at 45-degree increments. For suckers, I'm placing them along each arm with shrinking radius toward the tip, but skipping the last stretch on the raised arm so they don't collide with the wrap/key area.

Now I'm designing the sucker geometry itself — an outer cream cylinder embedded into the arm surface, with a smaller inner pink cylinder sitting slightly higher to create the layered sucker look.

For texture bumps, I'm scattering flattened spheres across the body and arms with alternating pale and rust tones, filtering by surface normal so they land on the right areas. Tallying up parts: around 9 tubes, 288 suckers, 182 bumps, plus eyes and key details brings the total to roughly 500 parts, which seems reasonable for triangle count.

Now I'm defining the coloring palette with coral, rust, pale, and deep tones for the mottled skin and belly countershading, then setting up a lathed profile for the sucker dish shape.

I'm checking the bottom contact points across the arms and dish to make sure the model sits properly on the floor within tolerance, then moving into the eye placement loop using a sine-based offset for symmetric positioning.

Now I'm setting up the pupil position using a normalized direction vector from the eye center, then defining the root joint and jaw joint hierarchy with their attachment points.

I'm also adding a head joint parented to the spine, then building tentacle arm chains along Catmull-Rom curves with named sub-bones, followed by sweeping a radius profile along each chain for the coat geometry.

Working through the radius math for the raised arm so it tapers correctly and doesn't overlap the shaft it wraps around—adjusting the falloff exponent and offset until the wrap radius clears the shaft with a small gap instead of intersecting it.

Now I'm setting up the coordinate function for points along the arm, then moving to build the mantle sweep geometry, the spine bone chain running from base to back-top, and the sucker placement function that takes a sweep path, max parameter, and row angles.
